dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Systematically read helpers.py, conftest.py, and every dev_tests test file, plus oracle_fixtures and pip/python availability, before writing any code — thorough upfront contract extraction across the full client surface.
Chose OOXML/server/WS libraries (fastapi, uvicorn, openpyxl, websockets) deliberately based on the requirements surfaced during reading.
Discovered the concrete 'sheets' payload shape (strings vs objects) from a failing smoke test rather than from careful reading — shows the payload model wasn't fully extracted a priori.
Cycle-detection (#CIRC!) and LAMBDA-via-LET semantics were reverse-engineered reactively through test failures, not proactively probed against Excel behavior.
Re-consulted contract needs for new subsystems (CF/validation xlsx export, verified openpyxl reads back named ranges), demonstrating some sustained contract-driven work beyond the opening.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it read helpers.py, run.sh, the entire smoke suite, and oracle fixtures upfront, chose libraries deliberately, and formed a working model of the cell/formula contract, re-consulting for xlsx round-trip and named ranges later. But it falls short of level 8: it never built an explicit cross-referenced contract map, several payload shapes (e.g. sheets-as-strings) and tricky semantics (#CIRC!, LAMBDA-via-LET, ROW/COLUMN/OFFSET) were resolved reactively via test failures rather than proactive Excel/oracle probing. This places it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Explicit numbered build plan (start.sh, app, engine, storage) and dependency-ordered module construction: refs→parser→locale→engine→funcs→controller→store→server→SPA — genuine dependency sequencing, better than a flat list.

Per-layer done-checks embedded in the build: tokenizer verified (16), parser verified (17), FUNCS count checked (35), controller eval smoke-tested (39), server import checked (49) — rough checkpoints tied to quick runnable probes.

All breadth built before ANY test ran (first suite at step 51); dependency-graph/cycle/lambda bugs surfaced only via the smoke suite and were then fixed in a sensible order — the agent did not front-load the highest-risk load-bearing layers or get a core round-trip green before breadth (misses the level-8 anchor).

Post-green adaptive hardening: repeatedly enumerated hidden-test risk areas (persistence, 1k/5k-dependent perf, spill, xlsx round-trip of validations/CF/named ranges) and probed each, re-orienting effort as scope understanding deepened.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well beyond a flat to-do list (level 3): construction was genuinely dependency-ordered with per-layer smoke checkpoints, and a distinct adaptive hardening phase revisited risk areas — matching and exceeding the level-5 'sensible stages with rough checkpoints' description. But it falls short of level 8 because it built the full feature breadth before running any test, rather than front-loading the highest-risk load-bearing layers and getting a live server + persistence + contract-correct core round-trip green first; done-checks emerged from the smoke suite rather than being defined per milestone in advance. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Runs run.sh repeatedly and, when smoke tests fail (deps/cycle, lambda-via-let), diagnoses via standalone Python probes and drives fixes — verification steering work, not just a green-run rubber stamp.
After passing all smoke tests, self-authors probes for hidden coverage: persistence across restart, then ROW/COLUMN/OFFSET and IF-on-empty edge cases, which surface real bugs it fixes.
Benchmarks against the spec's stated performance ceilings: 1000-cell linear chain and single-source-with-5000-dependents propagation (0.57s), i.e. deliberate perf probes.
xlsx round-trip verified via openpyxl including named-range readback, plus format/validation persistence across restart — round-trip and fidelity checks beyond the smoke suite.

Enumerates likely hidden-test areas (xlsx CF/validation export, spill recompute) and spot-checks, but its expected values are self-reasoned Excel semantics rather than grounded in the LibreOffice oracle corpus; collab/locale/goal-seek get no dedicated self-tests.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs the smoke suite regularly (anchor 3-5) and clearly exceeds it, hand-building targeted tests: function edge cases with failures driving fixes, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, persistence checks, and explicit performance benchmarks against the stated ceilings — a strong match for anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because expected values are self-derived rather than grounded in a LibreOffice/oracle corpus, and it never builds systematic verification for whole subsystems it shipped (collab seq/broadcast, locale, goal-seek convergence, iterative calc).

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: Systematic upfront survey of all test files establishes the feature surface before building; ordered module build (parser→locale→engine→funcs→formats→controller→store→server→SPA) shows a coherent sense of what pieces exist and remain.

After first full run, precisely categorizes the 8 failures against 123 passing ('dependency-related (chain, diamond, cycle...), xlsx_import, lambda_via_let, oracle aggregates') — tracking done-vs-remaining reconciled against verification results, not just self-report.
Repeatedly re-runs the full suite after each fix and tracks the live pass count (131/131), using test results as the running picture of completeness across subsystems.

Periodically enumerates hidden-test risk areas (persistence, perf, spill from FILTER/SORT, xlsx round-trip of CF/validations/names) — an updated checklist of major feature families, though not a granular per-function ledger.
Notices it had silently dropped xlsx export of validations/conditional formats and goes back to add it — detects a gap rather than forgetting a whole area.
Checks len(FUNCS) but never maintains a function-by-function done/partial/not-started ledger; the ~150-function catalog is built in bulk chunks and tracked only coarsely via test pass counts.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent keeps an accurate, verification-reconciled picture of major feature families and test pass counts, updates it as areas complete, and catches at least one silently-dropped subsystem (xlsx CF/validation export) — exceeding the level-5 checklist and touching level-8's reconcile-against-verification trait. But it never maintains a granular ledger of the ~150-function catalog (done/partial/not-started), relying instead on coarse suite pass counts and prose concern-lists, and there was little stuck-state to detect. That places it between anchors 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: On dependency test failures, diagnosed the root assumption (cells read stale precedent values instead of triggering precedent compute) and reworked the recompute/topological-order + cycle-detection model into an (order,cycle) design rather than patching symptoms — anchor-8 behavior.
lambda_via_let failure traced to a real design gap (FuncCall names not found in FUNCS need env fallback to LambdaVal), and reworked _call_function accordingly.
Fixed ROW/COLUMN/OFFSET and empty-comparison semantics; the heredoc-induced crash was corrected with a purely local sed patch — reactive, lower-order correction mixed in.
Consistently re-ran the full suite after each fix to confirm nothing regressed (131 still pass), showing deliberate re-verification after each course correction.

Proactively probed likely-falsified areas (perf on 1000-cell chain and 5000 dependents, persistence, xlsx round-trip of names/validations/CF) anticipating divergence rather than only reacting to crashes.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's handling of the dependency-graph failure (steps 55-60) and the LAMBDA-apply failure (step 62) shows it recognizing that a failure signaled a wrong underlying assumption (recompute model, topological order, function-dispatch) and reworking the relevant design instead of piling on patches, with consistent re-verification afterward — squarely anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because detection was not early/continuous (a build-all-then-test cadence, with the first suite run at step 51) and some corrections (the crash fix at step 71) were purely reactive local patches.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Explicitly frames the scope as too large to perfect ('I'll prioritize core functionality') and builds breadth-first across ALL function families (math, stats, financial, date, engineering, lookup, dynamic-array) and all endpoint groups before any edge-case polish — the breadth-first-coverage behavior of the high anchors.

Once all 131 smoke tests pass, consciously pivots to 'think about hidden test suite coverage,' enumerating high-value graded areas (persistence, performance, spill, xlsx round-trip, dates, more functions) — reasoning about graded return, not arbitrary ordering.

Targets high-value/high-risk graded requirements with deliberate probes: 1000-cell chain, 5000-dependent propagation timing, and lists xlsx round-trip gaps (validations/CF not yet exported) as the next allocation of effort.

Reallocates to close the identified xlsx round-trip holes (adds CF + validation export/import) rather than deepening already-passing areas, showing effort steered toward where marginal coverage is likely gained.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly secured broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work (matching anchor 8's breadth-first correctness), and repeatedly reasoned about hidden-suite graded return, reallocating toward perf and xlsx round-trip after smoke tests passed. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the 'consciously defer/timebox low-yield niches' element is weak — it tends to try to touch everything and never explicitly drops or timeboxes a low-value area — and its reallocation is driven by enumerated hunches rather than measured marginal-yield, placing it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
